# `port/ports`

History by request, live by subscription, and a description of what a channel offers.
`isHistoryPort` and `isLivePort` are how a host asks which halves an adapter actually brought — a
port with a silent live channel is legitimate, and the workspace says so rather than failing.

## Example

```ts
import type { MarketDataPort } from 'lightweight-magic-charts';

export const port: MarketDataPort = {
  fetchBars: async () => ({ bars: [], exhausted: true }),
  describe: () => [],
  subscribe: () => () => undefined,
};
```

- **`FrameSink`** · type · `interface FrameSink { onFrame: (frame: Frame) => void; onStatus: (status: LinkStatus) => void }`
- **`HistoryPort`** · type · `interface HistoryPort { fetchBars: (req: HistoryRequest) => Promise<HistoryResult> }`
- **`HistoryRequest`** · type · `interface HistoryRequest { scope: Scope; from: number; to: number; barCount?: number | undefined; signal: AbortSignal }`
- **`HistoryResult`** · type · `interface HistoryResult { bars: readonly Bar[]; series?: ReadonlyMap<SeriesId, readonly Point[]> | undefined; exhausted: boolean; nextAvailable?: number | undefined }`
- **`isHistoryPort`** · value · `(p: unknown) => p is HistoryPort`
- **`isLivePort`** · value · `(p: unknown) => p is LivePort`
- **`LivePort`** · type · `interface LivePort { describe: (scope: Scope) => readonly ChannelDescriptor[]; subscribe: (scope: Scope, sink: FrameSink) => Unsubscribe }`
- **`MarketDataPort`** · type · `interface MarketDataPort { fetchBars: (req: HistoryRequest) => Promise<HistoryResult>; describe: (scope: Scope) => readonly ChannelDescriptor[]; subscribe: (scope: Scope, sink: FrameSink) => Unsubscribe }`
- **`Unsubscribe`** · type · `type Unsubscribe = () => void`
